findings.claim: The claimed ONE absolute 15 s deadline does not bound the connect phase or a stalled streaming body: the ureq agent is built once with timeout_connect(policy.timeout) and the deadline is only re-checked between hops, while read_capped blocks in read_to_end with no deadline check.

evidence.observation: AgentBuilder uses .timeout_connect(policy.timeout) once; per-hop only .timeout(remaining) is updated, so a slow DNS/connect on a later hop gets a fresh full window.
fetch computes remaining and checks the deadline only at the top of each hop loop; Hop::Body then calls read_capped(reader, cap) which reads to cap+1 with no intermediate deadline test.
read_capped does r.take(cap+1).read_to_end with no timeout parameter; a trickling body can keep the call inside one hop past the deadline.

findings.remedy: Derive timeout_connect from remaining per hop (or cap it at remaining) and enforce the absolute deadline inside the body read (chunked read with per-chunk deadline checks).
findings.trigger: A catalog redirect chain or body that stalls in DNS/connect or trickles one byte at a time; elapsed wall time exceeds 15 s while fetch reports no deadline error.
findings.verification: Serve a catalog whose second hop stalls 20 s in connect, and one whose body trickles; time the fetch and confirm both end by 15 s with a deadline error.

findings.claim: The 500-pair cap evicts the oldest recorded refusals, so 'stays refused in every later pass' is false once more than 500 pairs accumulate: merge_older drains from the front, keeping only the newest.

evidence.observation: merge_older appends new pairs then drains ..excess from the front; the capped test asserts only the newest are kept.

findings.remedy: Either keep refusals unbounded (small records), pin eviction to never drop pairs for currently-seated ids, or correct the claim/docs to 'the newest 500 refusals are remembered'.
findings.trigger: More than 500 distinct (seated, candidate) older-pairs accumulate; the earliest refusal is evicted and a re-stamped old model becomes a candidate again.
findings.verification: Seed state.older with 500 other pairs, add one more older pair for the seated id, and assert plan_swaps still refuses it.

findings.claim: The smoke's one-entry roster is written beside the scratch repo with a plain fs::write to a predictable sibling path and no exclusive create, so a pre-created symlink at that path redirects the write to an arbitrary file.

evidence.observation: Path is work.with_file_name(<work-basename>.roster.json) in the shared temp dir; fs::write follows symlinks; cleanup relies only on RemoveOnDrop of the same path.

findings.remedy: Create the bound-roster file exclusively (O_EXCL / create_new) inside the scratch workdir or a uniquely created temp dir, and fail closed if it already exists.
findings.trigger: A symlink exists at the expected sibling <work>.roster.json path when a Bind::Entry smoke starts; the write follows it.
findings.verification: Pre-create that sibling path as a symlink to a sentinel file, run a Bind::Entry smoke, and check the sentinel is unchanged.

findings.claim: bound_roster protection checks are narrower than 'never smoked': reserve_percent read via as_i64().unwrap_or(0) misses float/non-integer values, on_request requires literal boolean true, and the inactive match is exact case-sensitive provider/plan equality.

evidence.observation: reserve_percent uses .and_then(as_i64).unwrap_or(0) > 0, so 0.5 or "15" is treated as 0; on_request uses as_bool()==Some(true), so "true" passes; inactive compares trimmed exact strings only.

findings.remedy: Accept any numeric >0 (as_f64) for reserve_percent, any truthy on_request, and case-insensitive provider/plan matching consistent with roster validation.
findings.trigger: A roster entry carries "reserve_percent": 0.5 (float) or on_request as a string, or an inactive list with different case; bound_roster returns Ok and the seat is smoked.
findings.verification: Call bound_roster on fixtures with float reserve_percent, string on_request, and case-variant inactive entries and assert refusal.

findings.claim: A future date within the 24 h slack still seats an unanchored candidate: negative evidence only fires past now+86400 while the unanchored rule accepts anything >= now-180d, so clock skew or a +23 h stamp is believed.

evidence.observation: negative_evidence refuses future only when c > now + FUTURE_SLACK_SECS (86400).
Unanchored branch qualifies when c >= now - 180d, which a +23 h stamp satisfies; the within-slack test documents +3600 as believed.

findings.remedy: Refuse any candidate dated after now (plus a small minutes-scale skew allowance) in the qualifying branches, not only past 24 h.
findings.trigger: A catalog lists only the candidate with created = now + 23 h while the seated id is absent; plan_swaps returns it as a candidate.
findings.verification: Call plan_swaps with an unanchored candidate stamped now+23h and assert it is rejected, not a candidate.

reply_markdown:
Q1. Redirects now stay on the start host+port with no userinfo (`env.rs:352`, `web.rs:192`) and keys never follow (`Redirects::Never`). Residuals: (a) no SSRF guard — any configured https host, including IP literals/loopback/private nets, is fetchable and each hop re-resolves DNS with no pinning; (b) the 15 s deadline is checked only between hops while `timeout_connect` stays at the full window (`env.rs:163`) and `read_capped` streams with no deadline check — finding #1; (c) only `User-Agent: c3/<version>` is sent besides endpoint `Authorization` — no key on public GETs, but the version is identifying.

Q2. Hostile bodies look contained: ids must pass `valid_model_id` (ASCII, no quote/backslash/newline, ≤100) before storage/comparison/roster edit (`version.rs:90`, `web.rs:210`, `models.rs:797`); vendor slugs are restricted and `:variant`s dropped (`web.rs:245`); bodies over the cap parse to nothing. No roster/CLI/path injection found in this part.

Q3. Date gate is much stronger (negative evidence wins, both-dated own-list gate, recorded pairs). Residuals: the 500-pair cap evicts the oldest refusal so permanence is false (finding #2); a future stamp within 24 h still seats an unanchored candidate (finding #5); future refusals are not recorded so a hostile future stamp retries every pass (by design, noisy but safe).

Q4. Seat binding is real: `Bind::Entry` position check, fresh `basis` re-read, same-snapshot smoke+swap, one-entry roster removed on drop, `--dry-run` writes nothing (`mod.rs:780`, `models_pass:815`). Residuals: predictable sibling temp write with no exclusive create (finding #3); `Bind::Label` explicit overrides resolve by label with no protection check; narrow `bound_roster` type checks (finding #4).

Q5. Writer is good: parsed span, provider+old recheck, whole-literal JSON replacement, semantic re-parse equality, double `current==basis` check, atomic write, once-per-day backup (`models.rs:786`). Residual: a microsecond TOCTOU remains between the final re-read and the atomic rename — concurrent writers can still lose; also deep (>64) or BOM'd rosters fail closed (safe).

Q6. Newer-release path keeps the original `previous`, re-records before install, honours cool-down/`--force`/in-use, and smokes post-update (`mod.rs:1272`). No `C3_CHILD` issue attaches to this part's children beyond the scratch smoke repo. CHANGELOG overclaims only in Q3's 'every later pass' (false past 500) — otherwise the sentences match the code read.

Q7. Untested that matters: real catalog/redirecting host/`model_pages`/roster swap/vendor release/real reviewer CLI (brief says so); slow-connect/trickle bodies; 500-cap eviction; symlink-at-roster-path; float/string protection variants; crash between newer-record write and install (retries same target each pass); Windows temp/rename behaviour.

## Requested checks
RC1. Time a catalog fetch through a 20 s stalled second-hop connect and a 1-byte/s body (read-only config + local stub; needs network-loopback permission); observation settling finding #1: both must end by ~15 s with a deadline error. Budget: minutes.
RC2. Seed state.older with 500 pairs then add the (seated,candidate) pair and run plan_swaps (workspace-write for state fixture); observation settling finding #2: refusal must persist. Budget: minutes.
RC3. Pre-create the expected sibling `<work>.roster.json` symlink to a sentinel and run a Bind::Entry smoke (workspace-write temp only); observation settling finding #3: sentinel unchanged and smoke fails closed. Budget: minutes.
unproven: Whether ureq's per-request timeout actually aborts a mid-body stall on all platforms (read-only review could not execute it).
Whether the 500-pair eviction is reachable in practice before seated ids rotate (no live catalog history observed).
Whether temp-dir symlink planting is exploitable in the operators' real environments.
verdict_reason: The hardening is real, but the deadline, permanence, temp-write, and protection-check residuals above must be fixed or scoped before release.
